--- my note for further check - "Beta cholesterol" is the historical term Framingham used in early exam cycles (Original Cohort Exam 11 = 1950s–60s era) for LDL, typically derived via ultracentrifugation fractionation (separating alpha- and beta-lipoprotein bands), not a modern direct enzymatic assay. Mapping to a numbered "LDL 4" variant implies a specific contemporary method that almost certainly doesn't match a 1970s-era ultracentrifugation-based measurement — worth checking whether a general, method-unspecified LDL cholesterol code (e.g., LOINC:13457-7, "Cholesterol in LDL [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma") is more appropriate given the historical assay context, rather than a specific numbered method variant.
